newsitem.title: UK: London PGMs off highs, face further volatility.
newsitem.headline: London PGMs off highs, face further volatility.

text.p: Prices of platinum group metals (PGMs) on Monday were off the heights gained last week but dealers forecast volatile moves would continue.

Prices for the main PGMs platinum and palladium have risen dramatically this year and especially in the past couple of weeks due to administrative problems keeping exports from Russia off the market. Russia expects to begin shipping June 20
Meanwhile gold and silver prices having attracted some support from the PGMs, failed to progress from Friday's levels.
Gold fixed at $343.85 per ounce after $344.00 on Friday and silver was seven cents down from the close at $4.81/$4.83.
"It is difficult to see gold making much of a break out with the summer coming on and the market going into its seasonal lull," one dealer said.
Before the market would look more positive it would have to overcome likely producer forward selling between $345.00 and $348.00 -- the top end being a value not seen since mid May.
Silver has been attracting speculative interest which has caused moves in the one-three months contango recently.
One dealer said the halving of the nearby contango to two percent from four percent indicated a large short position had been established in the market.
"This is not physical tightness but short term speculation," the dealer said.
Speculation was also seen being behind platinum moves. "There is real tightness in palladium (supplies) due to the Russians but platinum is being manipulated," one dealer said.
PGM markets were quiet on Monday but threatened to be volatile if spreads flared from the morning's $5.00 to $30 as they were on Friday.
"You only have to do a couple of deals like that and the price moves $50-$60 dollars. People can take the price where they want for a few hundred ounces," one dealer said.
The effective end of a forward market could have long term repercutions for the business.
Quoting forward rates was reduced to a "suggestion" basis after one-month palladium lease rates ballooned to over 100-200 percent last week.
PGM users in the glass and oil industries have been encouraged to lease material rather than buy it as the material can be sent back to the PGM dealer for recylng after use.
"Without a forward market you can't make a lease rate and people are forced to buy metal at these prices. It wil damage the industry," a dealer said.
